one_liner: Salesforce has broad REST/SOAP/Bulk APIs with OAuth 2.0, a free Developer Edition org, and official hosted MCP servers; AppExchange partner terms add some friction.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 via External Client App or Connected App (auth code, client credentials, JWT bearer). SOAP login() with username+password+security token also exists (session ID).
access_notes: Free Developer Edition org has API enabled. Production use needs Enterprise+ editions (Professional needs an add-on). Trial orgs are not API enabled. Updated terms say apps generally must enroll in the AppExchange Partner Program, with exceptions.
blocker_notes: Each customer org must have API-enabled edition and an External/Connected App set up. AppExchange Partner Program enrollment may be required for distributed apps.

evidence.quote: it must be authorized as a safe visitor. To implement this authorization, use either an external client app or a connected app and an OAuth 2.0 authorization flow.
When a client app invokes the `login()` call, it passes in a username and password as credentials.
API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer Edition orgs. Professional Edition orgs can add API access as an add-on.
Developer Edition provides a free and easy solution so that you can use Salesforce for testing and development.
you may only access or use Salesforce services to develop, operate, authenticate, integrate to, or distribute your application if it is enrolled in the AppExchange Partner Program.
Bulk API 2.0 is a REST-based API that supports all OAuth 2.0 flows supported by other Salesforce REST APIs.
A hosted MCP server is a Salesforce-managed endpoint that exposes your org’s logic and assets — data, flows, Apex actions, queries, and more — to any AI client that speaks MCP.
